content: I'll read the test image to analyze the plant disease symptoms.

**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected part:** Stem — the image shows a cross-sectional/longitudinal view of a plant stem that has been split open or peeled back
- **Key symptoms:**
  - The stem exterior is green but shows streaking and discoloration
  - **Internal brown/tan streaking and discoloration** of the vascular tissue running lengthwise along the stem
  - The internal tissue shows a **brownish, water-soaked, rotted appearance** — the pith and vascular bundles appear necrotic/discolored
  - The surrounding plant tissue (leaves, etc.) is **wilted and dead (brown, desiccated)**
  - The plant appears completely collapsed/wilted
  - The stem is on black plastic mulch, typical of tomato/solanaceous crop production
  - No obvious fungal mycelium, sclerotia, or lesion patterns visible on the exterior
  - The internal browning is streaky and longitudinal — characteristic of **vascular wilt**

**Differential Reasoning:**

- The **internal vascular browning** of the stem is the key diagnostic feature here
- **Verticillium Wilt** causes internal brown streaking in vascular tissue with plant wilting — very consistent with this image
- **Bacterial Wilt / Southern Bacterial Wilt** can also cause internal discoloration but often presents with bacterial ooze
- **Sclerotinia Timber Rot** would show white cottony mycelium and black sclerotia inside the stem
- **Southern Blight** would show white mycelium/sclerotia at the soil line
- The longitudinal brown streaking in the vascular/pith tissue with whole-plant wilt strongly points to **Verticillium Wilt**
